key_insight: PatientAgentBench shows that patient-facing health AI agents can look strong on static tests yet still make unsafe or incomplete decisions in realistic, tool-using conversations.
clinical_relevance: For primary care and triage support, the benchmark highlights persistent risks in screening, safety, and workflow accuracy that matter for patient-facing AI deployment.
method: Benchmarked 10 models across 4 model families on 1,200 patient scenarios.
Used a sandboxed agent with healthcare tools to converse with simulated patients.
Scored conversations with an LLM-as-a-Jury across 6 clinician-grounded dimensions, then validated against licensed clinician annotations.
evidence_signal: Clinician validation showed 79–93% adjacent agreement with the jury, and model performance ranged from 32% to 88% on triage quality, with the strongest model reaching only 4.25/5 overall.
watch_item: Results come from simulated conversations and tool environments, so real-world deployment still needs careful monitoring for missed emergencies, unverified tool outputs, and administrative actions taken without clinical screening.
paper_title: PatientAgentBench: A Benchmark Framework for Evaluating Patient-Facing Health AI Agents
